title: Night shift work exposure shapes neurobehavioral and cardiometabolic profiles in female healthcare workers: a cross-sectional study.
reason: Reported cardiometabolic outcomes are BMI, waist-to-height ratio, METS-IR, TyG, WyG and IRCV. These are not the review's prespecified standard MetS components (waist circumference/central obesity, blood pressure, fasting glucose, triglycerides, HDL) and the report does not appear to diagnose MetS.
recommended_action: Do not synthesize until outcome eligibility is formally adjudicated.

title: Effectiveness of a Food Education Program for healthcare workers: a pilot study in a Total Worker Health approach.
reason: Reported improvements include BMI, waist-to-hip ratio, HbA1c, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and vitamin D. These do not map cleanly to the prespecified MetS component rule; HbA1c is not fasting glucose and waist-to-hip ratio is not the prespecified waist-circumference criterion.
recommended_action: Do not synthesize as MetS-component evidence unless the eligibility rule is explicitly broadened.

title: Mental stress and the risks of metabolic syndrome and related components in military personnel: CHIEF cohort study.
reason: BSRS-5 measures general mental distress rather than explicitly occupational/job stress. The population is occupational, but the exposure may fall outside the review's prespecified occupational-stress construct.
recommended_action: Keep provisional pending exposure-scope adjudication; do not pool with job-stress studies yet.
